takeaway: An acute transfusion reaction is a type II hypersensitivity reaction: circulating IgG and IgM antibodies react with antigens on cell surfaces. Type I is IgE-mediated allergy.

question.text: An 85-year-old man develops an acute transfusion reaction after a transfusion for lower GI bleeding. Which hypersensitivity type is it?

lines.text: Our patient is bleeding, so he is given a blood transfusion.
Soon after, he has an acute transfusion reaction.
Look at the red cells: their surface carries antigens.
Circulating IgG and IgM antibodies attack those cell surface antigens.
That is the Type Two hypersensitivity shield.
Rhesus incompatibility works the same way.
Type One is different: it is allergy, with IgE on mast cells, like a bee sting.
So a transfusion reaction is Type Two.
